diagnostic_evidence.quote:
At time step n, second-order Strang splitting \cite{strang1968construction} is 
shown as:

issues.failure_explanation: The displayed composition consists of backward Euler, forward Euler, and backward Euler steps. Symmetric ordering does not make these first-order subsolvers second-order. In particular, when S vanishes, the displayed algorithm is simply forward Euler. The higher-order solvers introduced later are not the updates specified by these identities.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Write the splitting diagram using subproblem solution operators, and explicitly substitute the later SDIRK2 and higher-order SSP-RK integrations when asserting second-order accuracy. Retain the stated qualification about the first-order fallback.
issues.overall_effect: The displayed construction does not have its stated second-order temporal accuracy.
issues.title: The displayed Strang update uses first-order Euler substeps
issues.why_classification: The required higher-order subsolvers already appear later in the source, so a local correction of the splitting specification preserves the intended method and its attainable order.

diagnostic_evidence.quote:
In single-phase flow regions, 
    since steps 1 and 3 can be bypassed, 
    the algorithm effectively reduces to step 2 alone.

successfully stabilizes two-phase flow cases in the paper and 
locks the splitting errors at the interfaces,

issues.failure_explanation: The argument establishes only that no local source update is needed where kappa vanishes. It does not establish confinement of accumulated errors. Outside the special pressure-velocity equilibrium, splitting errors in volume fraction perturb pressure through the EOS. The momentum and energy fluxes then transmit those errors into pure-phase regions, including along acoustic waves. Such regions can consequently inherit second-order temporal errors.

failure_location.quote:
Therefore, the second-order limitation of Strang splitting is thus localized to the temporal precision 
    at the two-phase interface, while 
    preserving high-order fidelity in the smooth, single-phase regions.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Restrict the assertion to local error generation and to single-phase domains of dependence unaffected by mixed-region errors; remove the claim that splitting errors remain locked at interfaces.
issues.overall_effect: The claimed interface confinement and higher global temporal accuracy throughout smooth single-phase regions are unsupported.
issues.title: Vanishing source terms do not confine splitting errors to interfaces
issues.why_classification: A meaningful local or domain-of-dependence statement survives, but the regional global-error guarantee must be weakened. The numerical update and its overall second-order description need not change.

issues.failure_explanation: Continuity is neither assumed nor guaranteed by the Tammann formulas. Take gamma_1=gamma_2=2, p_w,1=0, p_w,2=1, fixed internal-energy density 3/2, z^n=1/2, and Delta t_im div(u)=-3. The initial pressure is 1/2>0. Along the source step, p(z)=2z-1/2 and kappa(z)=z(1-z)/(3z-1/2), which has a genuine pole at z=1/6. The implicit equation would require (z-1/2)(3z-1/2)=-3z(1-z), hence z=-1/4. Thus no solution in [0,1] exists, even after removable singularities are cancelled. Endpoint signs can make bisection converge to a pole rather than a root.

failure_location.quote:
The continuity of $F(z_1)$ guarantees the 
existence of root $z_1^{n+1} \in [0, 1]$.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: No complete source-supported repair identified; at minimum, a repair must establish a pole-free valid root bracket and a root-selection rule throughout the claimed regime, or explicitly abandon the unconditional gas-liquid guarantee.
issues.overall_effect: The backward-Euler existence theorem, the proposed bisection implementation, and the inherited unconditional volume-fraction BP guarantee of the adaptive implicit solver fail for admissible gas-liquid input data.
issues.title: The implicit source function can have poles and no bounded root
issues.why_classification: The theorem is false even for initially positive-pressure states. Adding continuity, energy-range, or small-step restrictions would remove part of the advertised unconditional regime; retaining that regime requires a different source-step construction or analysis.

diagnostic_evidence.quote:
When we use the DG($P^K$) method for variable $\mathbf{U}$, 
the expected spatial accuracy for the velocity field $\mathbf{u}$ is $\mathcal{O}(\Delta x^{K+1})$.

issues.failure_explanation: Consider K=1 on a uniform one-dimensional mesh, embedded in the stated Cartesian setting, with constant density and positive smooth velocity u=C+x^2. Its cellwise L2 projection is u_h=C+x_i^2+h^2/12+2x_i(x-x_i), an O(h^2) approximation. These projected traces agree across interfaces, so the proposed numerical flux introduces no lifting correction. The reconstructed derivative is therefore D_h=2x_i, whereas u_x=2x; its maximum error is h, not O(h^2). Additional superconvergence or reconstruction assumptions are necessary.

failure_location.quote:
To recover the optimal $(K+1)$-th order accuracy for the divergence 
term, inspired by the LDG method \cite{cockburn1998local}, we employ the following reconstruction procedure to 
obtain a approximation $D_h\approx \nabla\cdot\mathbf u$.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Withdraw the automatic order-restoration guarantee and describe the formula only as a weak derivative reconstruction. Retaining the claimed order requires a different reconstruction or a proved additional approximation property of the actual DG velocity.
issues.overall_effect: The asserted optimal spatial accuracy of the reconstructed source divergence, and the claimed restoration of optimal source-term precision, are not established by this procedure.
issues.title: The weak divergence reconstruction does not automatically restore optimal order
issues.why_classification: The stated input accuracy permits a full order loss, including only first-order divergence accuracy for P1. The source supplies no comparable construction or estimate preserving the advertised optimal rate.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: The solution after BP limiter satisfies \eqref{U_ingp} and maintain the element average of the OEDG solution.

issues.failure_explanation: The two cases overlap, and selecting the lower-bound factor need not enforce the upper bound. For example, mean z=0.5, minimum -0.1, and maximum 1.5 give a lower-bound factor approximately 5/6, leaving the limited maximum approximately 4/3. Such data occur for the quadratic z(xi)=0.4+0.8xi+0.3xi^2 on [-1,1]. Constant positive partial densities and constant pressure can make all other limiting factors equal to one.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Compute separate lower- and upper-bound factors, using one for an inactive constraint, and take their minimum together with one.
issues.overall_effect: The limiter can leave quadrature-point volume fractions outside [0,1], despite an admissible cell average.
issues.title: The volume-fraction limiter fails when both bounds are violated
issues.why_classification: Taking the minimum of the two required factors is a routine local correction preserving conservation, common-factor limiting, and the intended bounds.

issues.failure_explanation: Convexity of the positive-pressure set does not imply concavity of pressure itself. With gamma_1=2, gamma_2=3, zero reference pressures and velocity, and constant positive partial densities summing to one, take z=1/2+xi/4 and E=3/4-13xi/8. The mean-state pressure is 1 and the minimum pressure is -1 at xi=1, so the prescribed factor is approximately 1/2. The resulting pressure at that point is approximately -1/13, still negative. The variable EOS denominator invalidates the pressure-chord estimate underlying the formula.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Apply the same scaling construction to the concave residual Q(U)=E-|m|^2/(2rho)-B(z)-epsilon_p A(z), where A and B are the EOS denominator and background-pressure term. Use the minimum of Q over the quadrature points to select the factor.
issues.overall_effect: The pressure limiter can fail even when the cell average is admissible and Step 1 has already enforced all density and volume-fraction bounds.
issues.title: The pressure scaling factor incorrectly treats pressure as concave
issues.why_classification: The needed concavity is already established in the convexity proof, and subtracting epsilon_p times the affine denominator preserves it. Replacing pressure values by this residual is a local repair without changing the substantive guarantees.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: The solution after BP limiter satisfies \eqref{U_ingp} and maintain the element average of the OEDG solution.

We note that our framework will be a BP-OEDG scheme for five equation transport model 
when we omit step 1 and step 3.
For all cases, we simply employ $\Delta t \propto \Delta x$ and $CFL=0.1$.

issues.failure_explanation: Mean-preserving limiting cannot put all positive-weight quadrature states in the convex set Gp when their mean lies outside Gp. The transport update can produce precisely this failure under a normal CFL. For the admitted P0 specialization, set gamma_1=gamma_2=2, reference pressures 0 and 1, constant z=1/2, density 1, pressure epsilon=0.001, and velocities (-a,0,a) in three adjacent cells, with a=0.1. Write c=sqrt(1+2epsilon), S=a+c, and lambda=Delta t/h. The stated Lax-Friedrichs update gives central momentum zero, unchanged z, and p_new=epsilon-lambda*a*c*(c-a/2). At lambda*S=0.1 this is approximately -0.00765, while partial densities stay positive. No average-preserving limiter can repair this cell. This counterexample uses no implicit source step and survives correction of both limiter factors.

failure_location.quote:
2. Strang Splitting Step 2 : &DG solver for Eq. \ref{eq:RHS} $(\Delta t)$&  
   \textbf{OEDG+BP limiter} \\

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: No complete source-supported repair identified; at minimum, a repair must guarantee admissible cell averages before every limiting stage. This requires an appropriate invariant-domain update, state-dependent step restriction or rejection, or a change to the positivity and conservation guarantees.
issues.overall_effect: The claimed pressure-BP property of the transport variant and the stage-wise BP justification for the full computational procedure fail. Convexity of Gp alone does not provide the missing cell-average invariant.
issues.title: The algorithm does not preserve the admissible cell averages required by its limiters
issues.why_classification: The necessary pressure-dependent step bound can tend to zero as pressure approaches zero relative to the reference pressure. Imposing it can forfeit the advertised standard-CFL operation; merely correcting the pointwise limiters cannot restore the guarantee.

issues.failure_explanation: The first proposed witness has z_2 rho_2=0 and the second has z_1 rho_1=0, whereas G requires both partial densities to be strictly positive. Neither witness belongs to the stated set. Their midpoint therefore does not, as written, demonstrate non-convexity of G.

failure_location.quote:
Thus, $\mathbf{U}^{(1)}$ is physically 
 admissible and belongs to $\mathcal{G}$.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: For sufficiently small positive delta, replace the witnesses by [1.2(1-delta),1000delta,0,1000,1-delta] and [1.2delta,1000(1-delta),0,6001,delta]. Their midpoint is unchanged, their partial densities are positive, and the endpoint sound-speed signs persist by continuity.
issues.overall_effect: Appendix A does not supply its claimed counterexample for the admissible set actually defined in the paper.
issues.title: The non-convexity witnesses are excluded by the stated admissible set
issues.why_classification: A routine perturbation and continuity check repairs the witnesses while preserving the non-convexity conclusion and all other claims.
